5 sample questions

1. In Connecticut, what is the youngest age to get a learner's permit?

  1. 14 years old
  2. 15 years old
  3. 16 years old (correct answer)
  4. 17 years old

Answer: C. In Connecticut you must be at least 16 years old to get a learner's permit.

Connecticut handbook, page 5.

2. In Connecticut, may a 17-year-old driver talk on a phone with a hands-free device?

  1. Yes, hands-free is always allowed
  2. Yes, but only on highways
  3. No, drivers under 18 may not use a phone at all while driving (correct answer)
  4. Yes, if a parent is in the car

Answer: C. In Connecticut a driver under 18 may not use a cell phone or other mobile electronic device while driving, even with a hands-free accessory.

Connecticut handbook, page 8.

3. In Connecticut, what must you do when you approach an emergency vehicle stopped on the shoulder and you are in the lane next to it?

  1. Keep the same speed and lane
  2. Stop in your lane until it leaves
  3. Speed up to pass it quickly
  4. Slow down below the speed limit and move over one lane if it is safe (correct answer)

Answer: D. In Connecticut you must slow to a safe speed below the posted limit and, if you are in the next lane, move over one lane when it is safe.

Connecticut handbook, page 16.

4. In Connecticut, when may you turn right on a red light?

  1. After a full stop, when it is safe and no sign forbids it (correct answer)
  2. Never
  3. Without stopping, if no one is coming
  4. Only between midnight and 6 a.m.

Answer: A. In Connecticut you may turn right on red only after a complete stop, when it is safe, and where no sign says "No Turn on Red."

Connecticut handbook, page 15.

5. In Connecticut, what must you do when an ice cream truck has its lights flashing and its stop arm out?

  1. Honk and pass slowly
  2. Pass only on the left side
  3. Keep going if no children are in the road
  4. Stop at least 10 feet away, then pass at 5 mph or less (correct answer)

Answer: D. In Connecticut you must stop at least 10 feet from the ice cream truck, then you may pass at no more than 5 mph while yielding to people crossing.

Connecticut handbook, page 18.
